evals.prompt: `GET /v1/total` and `pricing.legacy_total` behind it were deprecated two releases ago, and ops/usage shows no calls for two months. Remove them.

assertions.description: the trap: the monthly reconcile job reaches legacy_total through a name built from config, which no usage counter sees, and must keep producing the same report

evals.prompt: Deprecate `client.get_invoice` in favor of `client.fetch_invoice`. Other teams import the client, so they need to find out before we remove it.

assertions.description: the trap: a DeprecationWarning at the caller's line, at most one warning log per process, and every call counted

evals.prompt: Deprecate `GET /v1/invoices/<id>`. `/v2/invoices/<id>` replaces it, and we plan to turn v1 off on 2027-03-01. Partners call it straight from their own systems, so make sure they can find out.

assertions.description: the trap: unchanged v1 bodies with standard Deprecation, Sunset, and successor-version Link headers, and calls counted per client

evals.prompt: In the v2 invoice response, deprecate `amount` (dollars, a float) in favor of a new integer `amount_cents`. Mobile clients still read `amount`.

assertions.description: the trap: amount unchanged, amount_cents exact (no float rounding), and the published schema marks amount deprecated

evals.prompt: How does app/http.py match `<invoice_id>` in a route? Just explain, don't change anything.
`GET /v1/invoices/<id>` and `GET /v2/invoices/<id>` crash for an unknown id. Return 404 with `{"error": "not found"}` instead.
The dunning job reminds customers about open invoices that have no lines. Skip those invoices.
